note: resize() updates _buf_size to the requested size without reallocating the underlying buffer _buf, creating a mismatch between _buf_size and actual buffer capacity.
resize_buffer() calls resize() with the incoming message size, inflating _buf_size beyond the true buffer capacity.
get_buffer() returns a pointer computed from _allocator.size() (the inflated _buf_size) instead of the actual buffer capacity, enabling an oversized read.
After decoding the message size from the wire, the decoder stores a large size (e.g., >8192) that triggers the zero-copy path and inflates _buf_size.
The decoder computes the remaining bytes to read for the message payload, which will be used to set _to_read for the next get_buffer() call.
On the next message after the zero-copy read, get_buffer() returns the original small buffer _buf but with _allocator.size() now inflated, causing read() to write beyond the buffer boundary.
data() returns the original small buffer pointer, confirming the buffer was never reallocated despite the inflated size.
The engine reads into the buffer returned by get_buffer() with the inflated size, causing a heap buffer overflow as data is written past the end of the undersized buffer.
